cover.dek: The Shidid family civil war continues, the prodigy comes for the master and half the league’s stars are on vacation. Week 6 predictions, analysis and Oscar’s picks.
cover.headline: Brother vs. Brother

games.lineText: (1–4) Baby Abdo - Jackson 🖐️ (+205) vs. (1–4) Shmoody - I Can’t Breathe (−255)
locker: Baby Abdo
Mo got me last week. Shmoody gets me this week? No. Somebody in this family is losing to me, and it’s starting Sunday.
Shmoody
Little bro wants smoke? Big brother strength is different. Two-game win streak starts Sunday. And Oscar, don’t say a word.
games.oscarNote: Oscar said nothing. Oscar has met the family.
games.spreadText: Spread: Shmoody −16.5 | Adjusted Projection: Baby Abdo 104.8 - Shmoody 121.3
story: Last week the oldest brother broke the league record against him. This week Baby Abdo gets the other one.

Nobody in the Shidid family has had a worse October than Abdo. He walked into Week 5 against Mo, ran into a record-setting 196.10 and spent the rest of the night being told to acknowledge his big brother. He has lost three straight, he sits last in the league in points scored at 584.98, and the family dinner table has never felt longer. Revenge on Mo will have to wait. Revenge on Shmoody is available on Sunday.

Shmoody is in no mood to be anybody’s consolation prize. The defending champion finally woke up last week, arrested Sean, burned a Florian Wirtz jersey and won his first game of the season. Now he wants a streak, and he wants to remind little bro that big brother strength is a different kind of strength. Brock Bowers, James Cook and Mike Evans are all rolling. His kicker is on bye, which is the only thing standing between him and a comfortable afternoon.

These two split their meetings last season, one win apiece. This is the rubber match, the family is watching, and one brother leaves Sunday with bragging rights while the other leaves with the dishes.
games.theme: Shidid Family Civil War, Part II
games.title: Baby Abdo vs. Shmoody: Can Little Brother Finally Get Even?

games.lineText: (4–1) Sean - CEEEDEEEZZZZ nuts (−225) vs. (3–2) Tyriese - Puka Nacua, 50% off (+185)
locker: Sean
Kenneth Walker has been located. Case closed. Somebody tell the King his crown is a rental.
Tyriese
Everybody wanted to talk about my draft. Now they want to talk about my crown. I’m gonna be king of the fantasy managers, and Sean’s just a stop on the map.
story: Two managers. Two rivalries that run both ways. And one man who finally has his running back back.

Last week Sean filed a missing person report for Kenneth Walker, got arrested by the defending champion and watched his perfect season leave in the back of a squad car. This week Walker is back from his bye, projected for 21.75, and Sean is projected for the most points in the league at 149.6. The case has been solved. The question is whether the damage is permanent.

Across the field stands King Tyriese, fresh off a 180.34-point raid and two straight wins. The preseason punchline now has Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Derrick Henry on the same ship, and a crown he has no intention of returning. He also beat Sean the only time they met, 104.64 to 100.66 in Week 6 last year.
Sean has the deeper roster. Tyriese has the momentum, the straw hat and a grudge. One of them leaves Sunday as the league’s most dangerous team. The other leaves with a very long Monday.
games.theme: The Case of the Missing Running Back
games.title: Sean vs. Tyriese: Can the King Dethrone the Former King?

watch.text: Fresh off the missing persons list and ready to make up for lost time.
The highest projection on either roster. The King’s first mate needs another 37.

games.lineText: (3–2) Tyler - Dolo’s cell mate (+310) vs. (4–1) Hogies - White Tyriese (−400)
locker: Tyler
I taught him everything he knows. Unfortunately, I also taught him to check bye weeks.
Hogies
He showed me the way. Now I’m showing him the door. Class is in session, and the teacher doesn’t have a quarterback.
games.spreadText: Spread: Hogies −24.5 | Adjusted Projection: Tyler 114.0 - Hogies 138.6
story: Every master eventually faces the student he created. Tyler taught Hogies how to play this game: how to read a waiver wire, how to work a trade, how to sleep through a 1 p.m. kickoff without checking his phone. On Sunday, the prodigy comes for the man who trained him.

The student has been flawless. Hogies is 4–1, sits at the top of Oscar’s power rankings and has Christian McCaffrey, Chris Olave and Trey McBride ready to go. He has also learned the most important lesson of all: let the other guy talk. Zach found that out the hard way last week.

The master, meanwhile, is riding a three-game winning streak and just declared a national holiday after beating the General. There is one small problem. Jared Goff and the Lions are on bye, and Tyler does not have another quarterback. We are adjusting his projection to 114 on the assumption that the teacher remembers his own first lesson: always have a backup.

The last time they met, the master won 144.80 to 94.02 in Week 11 last year. Hogies has not forgotten. He lists Tyler as a rival, and this is the week he finds out whether the student has truly become the master.
games.title: Hogies vs. Tyler: Can the Student Finally Beat the Teacher?

watch.text: 31.50 last week. The master needs his star pupil of a running back to cover for an empty quarterback slot.

locker: Tim
I got married, dropped 160, and I’m still the underdog? Fine. Coffee’s on me after.
Sgt. Bob
One loss. The army has been retrained. The honeymoon ends at 1300 hours.
games.spreadText: Spread: Sgt. Bob −8.0 | Projection: Tim 132.9 - Sgt. Bob 140.8
story: One week ago Tim got married and dropped 160.94 on Marissa. One week ago Sgt. Bob lost his first battle of the season. Both men arrive at Week 6 with something to prove.

The General has scored more points than anyone in the league, 736.30 through five weeks, and he treats every Sunday like a military operation. Losing to Tyler stung. The troops have reportedly been running drills ever since, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Kyren Williams and Brock Purdy are all projected for 21 or more.

Tim is still on his honeymoon. Christian Watson and Parker Washington combined for 62.70 points last week, and the Coffey Shop has won three of its last four. Tim lists Bob as a rival. These two have never played, which means the first shot of this war is fired on Sunday.
Bob is the favourite for a reason. But the General learned last week that his army can be beaten, and Tim has a way of surprising people on big weekends.
games.title: Tim vs. Sgt. Bob: Can the Newlywed Ambush the General?

watch.text: 32.30 at the wedding. The groom needs his best man again.
The General’s most decorated soldier and the top projected player on the field.

games.lineText: (1–4) Marissa - Tuten on my Little Saq (+105) vs. (1–4) Mo - Beazy (−125)
locker: Marissa
Everyone’s been talking about Mo’s 196. I’d like to talk about 2–4.
Mo
Chase and Jefferson are on vacation. I’m not. Somebody tell the league the record was a warm-up.
games.spreadText: Spread: Mo −2.5 | Adjusted Projection: Marissa 125.1 - Mo 127.8
story: Last week Mo set the league record with 196.10 and demanded the entire league acknowledge him. This week Ja’Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson are both on bye.

That is the problem with being the scariest 1–4 team in history: sometimes your scariest players take the week off. Mo still has Josh Allen, the top projected player in the game at 24.87, and enough depth to field a respectable lineup. Respectable is not 196.

Marissa scored 137.34 last week and lost anyway, then watched Mo post the best score the league has ever seen. She now has Drake Maye and Patrick Mahomes on the same roster and one quarterback slot to put them in. She also beat Mo the last time they met, 161.62 to 112.54 in Week 5 last year.
Two 1–4 teams. One gets to start climbing. The other gets to start explaining.
games.title: Marissa vs. Mo: Can the Record Breaker Do It Without His Stars?

watch.text: 39.46 last week. If he does it again, the spa can finally close.

games.lineText: (2–3) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+750) vs. (3–2) Zach - Trade God (−1300)
locker: Collin
My lawyer advised me not to comment. My lawyer is also my waiver claim.

I’m not saying anything until Monday night. Okay, one thing. It’s gonna feel good.
story: The last time Zach felt good about a matchup, he said so at 1 p.m. and lost at midnight. He has now lost two straight, and the clown makeup has barely come off.

Lucky for the Trade God, he has drawn the friendliest spot of the week. Collin is without Jahmyr Gibbs, who is on bye, and the waiver wire he sued last week has not settled out of court. His lineup projects for 104.2, the lowest in the league.

Zach, meanwhile, has Bijan Robinson projected for 25.43 and a roster built from the Kittle heist. These two list each other as rivals and have never met. On paper it is the biggest mismatch of the week, which is exactly when Zach is most dangerous to himself.
The line is 41 points. The only thing that can beat Zach on Sunday is Zach on Sunday afternoon.
games.title: Collin vs. Zach: Can the Trade God Stop Talking Until Monday?

games.lineText: (1–5) Shmoody - I Can’t Breathe (−405) vs. (2–4) Mo - Beazy (+310)
locker: Shmoody
I’ve been losing by a touchdown for a month. That ends Sunday. Mo, start whoever you want. It won’t matter.
Mo
Abdo got the record. Marissa got the warning. Shmoody gets the family finale. Somebody find me a quarterback.
games.oscarNote: Oscar is picking Mo on the assumption that he finds a quarterback. If he doesn’t, Oscar was never here.
games.spreadText: Spread: Shmoody −25.0 | Adjusted Projection: Shmoody 114.5 - Mo 116.0 (before Mo finds a quarterback)
story: Three brothers, three weeks, three games. Mo beat Baby Abdo in Week 5. Baby Abdo beat Shmoody in Week 6. Now the oldest and the middle brother settle the last piece of the family round robin, and somebody leaves with the dishes for good.

Shmoody is the defending champion, and he is 1–5. He has lost three games by less than a touchdown, and the latest came against his little brother, by 5.30 points, with 47.60 sitting on his bench. One more loss and a 1–6 record will make him a full-time spectator. Brock Bowers is still rolling, but James Cook and Mike Evans both project zero this week.

Mo is 2–4 and, by his own account, the scariest 2–4 team in history. He set the league record with 196.10 against Baby Abdo. He then beat Marissa without Ja’Marr Chase or Justin Jefferson. This week he has the opposite problem. Chase and Jefferson are healthy and sitting on his bench, and Josh Allen is on bye, the only quarterback on the roster. The sportsbook has taken his lineup at its word and made him a 25-point underdog.

This is also a fight for the head of the family table. Mo has mentioned the 196.10 at every meal since Week 5 and has reportedly asked for it to be engraved on the gravy boat. Shmoody points out that he is the one with the ring, which he now wears to dinner as a precaution. Baby Abdo is 1–1 against the pair this season and holding a framed box score. He has announced he will root for whoever makes the other one wash up.

If Mo starts his stars and finds a quarterback, this is a coin flip with a family dinner on the line. The last time these two met, Shmoody won 117.44 to 79.30. Mo has not forgotten. Neither has the group chat.

games.title: Shmoody vs. Mo: Who Owns the Family Dinner Table?

games.lineText: (5–1) Sean - CEEEDEEEZZZZ nuts (+200) vs. (4–2) Zach - Trade God (−250)
locker: Sean
I got the quarterback. He got a week of buyer’s remorse. See you Sunday.
Zach
I’m not saying anything until Monday. Okay, one thing. I won both trades.
story: At 12:08 Thursday morning, Sean and Zach made a trade. Twelve hours later Zach traded half of it away again. On Sunday the two men who started it all meet head to head.

Sean sits at No. 1 in the power rankings with the most points in the league, and he went shopping for a quarterback. He got Joe Burrow, one of the three quarterbacks this league actually values, plus DJ Moore and Zach Charbonnet. He paid with Zay Flowers and Matthew Stafford. Burrow scored 24.60 the last time he played. Moore is on bye.

Zach did not stop at one trade. He kept Flowers until lunchtime, then sent him to Tyler with Nico Collins and D’Andre Swift for Amon-Ra St. Brown, Aaron Jones and Luther Burden. He now starts Stafford, Bijan Robinson, St. Brown and George Kittle, and projects 140.2, the second-best number of the week.

The personal stakes are worse than the fantasy ones. Sean has spent a week at No. 1 and has started signing his group chat messages “Respectfully, the No. 1 team.” Zach is back at the pulpit with a new sermon, “How I Fleeced Two Men Before Lunch.” Neither man will admit he lost a trade, and only one of them can win on Sunday. The loser has to read the winner’s trade review in the group chat without replying. For Zach, that would be the longest silence of his career.
Last season Zach won this matchup 184.48 to 152.18. Sean has the better record. Zach has the better projection and a fresh set of toys. One of them is about to find out who won the trade.
games.title: Sean vs. Zach: Can the Trade God Beat the Man He Just Traded With?

watch.text: Bought to win weeks like this one. Scored 24.60 in Week 5 for the man he’s now playing against.
His third team in two weeks. Abdo had him, Tyler had him for a week, and now the Trade God has the WR4.

games.lineText: (3–3) Tyler - Dolo’s cell mate (−765) vs. (2–4) Collin - Annoyance of the league (+525)
locker: Tyler
Collin and I have done a lot of business. This is the first time I get to collect.
Collin
Everyone keeps telling me Gibbs is on my bench. I know. It’s called strategy.
games.oscarNote: Oscar has assumed Collin will notice Gibbs. Oscar has been wrong about Collin before.
games.spreadText: Spread: Tyler −34.5 | Adjusted Projection: Tyler 134.9 - Collin 134.3
story: Tyler and Collin have traded with each other twice in two weeks. In Week 5 Breece Hall went back to Collin, and Tyler took Luther Burden, Aaron Jones and Brian Robinson. In Week 6 Tyler sent Robinson back for Aaron Rodgers. Now they finally play each other, and almost nothing they swapped is still where they left it.

Tyler spent last week getting schooled by his own student, scoring a league-low 88.52. He answered by trading Amon-Ra St. Brown, a week after acquiring him, for Zay Flowers, Nico Collins, D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai. Burden and Jones went to Zach in the same deal. The new lineup projects 134.9, and three of his starters are less than a day old.

Collin has made seven trades and lost two straight. He picked up Kyler Murray on Wednesday and is starting him over Kirk Cousins, the quarterback he traded Stefon Diggs for. Jahmyr Gibbs, the RB1, is on his bench. So are A.J. Brown and Breece Hall.

Off the field, this is a relationship built on paperwork. Tyler and Collin have swapped so many players that their rosters should share a group chat, and Breece Hall has reportedly asked whose house he’s spending Sunday at. Tyler says he won every deal. Collin says he can’t remember the deals, which explains his bench. On Sunday they finally stop negotiating and start keeping score, and neither one is allowed to offer a trade to undo it.

That is why the line looks ridiculous. As set, Collin projects 100.3 and the book makes him a 34.5-point underdog. Start Gibbs, Brown and Hall, and he projects 134.3, a dead heat. The most important manager in this game is Collin’s lineup screen.
games.title: Tyler vs. Collin: Can the Old Trade Partners Settle the Account?

watch.text: His third team in twelve hours. Sean to Zach to Tyler, and he hasn’t had time to unpack.
The highest projection in the league, currently on the bench. Collin’s season may depend on noticing.

games.lineText: (5–1) Hogies - White Tyriese (+170) vs. (4–2) Tim - The Coffey Shop (−210)
locker: Hogies
Tuition is due Sunday. Tim, I accept Venmo.
Tim
Married life is undefeated. The academy is about to have its first dropout.
games.spreadText: Spread: Tim −13.0 | Adjusted Projection: Hogies 126.2 - Tim 132.0
story: One of them just opened a fantasy football academy. The other just got married and has not lost since.

Hogies is 5–1 and fresh off a 45-point lesson to the man who taught him the game. Enrollment at the academy is open. His lineup is a little less polished than his lectures, though. David Montgomery sits in a FLEX spot with a zero projection, and Tyler Shough is putting up points on his bench again.

Tim is 4–2 with two straight wins. He dropped 160.94 on Marissa the week of his wedding and then ambushed Sgt. Bob. Bo Nix, Ashton Jeanty, Chase Brown and Christian Watson give him one of the deepest lineups in the league, and the book has him favored by 13.

This is a clash of lifestyles. Hogies wants to talk about process: waiver theory, bye-week planning and a syllabus he has not shown anyone. Tim wants to talk about his wedding, and the wedding has been worth 286.38 points in two weeks. Hogies has offered Tim a place at the academy. Tim has offered Hogies a slice of leftover wedding cake. Only one of those offers is still fresh.
These two have never met. Somebody’s honeymoon or somebody’s semester ends on Sunday.
games.title: Hogies vs. Tim: Can the Academy Survive the Newlywed?

watch.text: The headmaster’s best student. Hogies needs a big day from him to cover the hole at FLEX.
118.80 points this season, more than any other player on Tim’s roster. The best wedding gift Tim has received.

games.lineText: (3–3) Tyriese - Puka Nacua, 50% off (−185) vs. (2–4) Baby Abdo - Jackson 🖐️ (+155)
locker: Tyriese
Henry owes me 75 points and an apology. He can start paying Sunday.
Baby Abdo
I beat my brother. I can beat a man who invoices running backs.
games.spreadText: Spread: Tyriese −10.5 | Projection: Tyriese 133.9 - Baby Abdo 123.4
story: Baby Abdo is coming off the biggest win of his season. Tyriese is coming off an invoice to Baltimore.

Abdo won the family rubber match last week, leads Shmoody 2–1 all time and has reportedly framed the box score for family dinner. He is also still living off the Week 6 deal that sent Amon-Ra St. Brown to Tyler. Bucky Irving, George Pickens, Jameson Williams and DK Metcalf all start for him this week. Lamar Jackson leads the way at quarterback.

Tyriese is 3–3 and holding a playoff spot. Derrick Henry gave him 5.00 points in Week 6, and Davante Adams wasn’t much better. Stefon Diggs, his prize from the Kirk Cousins trade, projects zero this week. Puka Nacua is still Puka Nacua, though, and the book makes Tyriese a 10.5-point favorite.

These two have spent the week sending paperwork. Tyriese has invoiced Baltimore for 75.72 bench points, and Abdo has mailed framed copies of his box score to every member of his family. Tyriese says the win over Shmoody was a family matter and doesn’t count. Abdo says a man who bills his own running back is in no position to judge. The loser has to write the winner a receipt.
Last season Abdo won this matchup 131.24 to 128.54. Expect it to be just as close.
games.title: Tyriese vs. Baby Abdo: Can the Spoils of the Amon-Ra Trade Pay Off?

watch.text: The best projection in the game and the reason his team name is still accurate.
One of the three quarterbacks this league respects. If little brother wins two straight, Lamar is why.

locker: Marissa

games.spreadText: Spread: Sgt. Bob −18.0 | Projection: Marissa 115.2 - Sgt. Bob 133.0

The General went from the top of the standings to two straight losses, and he has confined MarShawn Lloyd and Denzel Boston to barracks pending investigation. Boston is starting again anyway. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Kyren Williams and Brock Purdy give him a 133.0 projection, and the book has him favored by 18.

This is a grudge with a military file. The General has never forgotten last season’s 138.60 to 105.32 loss, and it is reportedly pinned to his war room wall next to a photo of Marissa labelled “Enemy Combatant No. 1.” Marissa insists she barely remembers the game. That, the General says, is exactly what an enemy combatant would say.
Marissa has the history. The General has the projection. Sunday decides which one goes in the tribunal’s official record.
games.title: Marissa vs. Sgt. Bob: Can the General Win a Battle?

body: Four weeks. Four losses. Four weeks of being called the biggest disappointment in fantasy football. Mo entered Week 5 with the weight of an entire preseason's worth of hype on his shoulders and a record that made him look less like a title contender and more like a man reserving a seat in the Toilet Bowl.
Then his little brother showed up. And apparently, that was all the motivation Mo needed.

In the most outrageous performance the league has ever witnessed, **Mo detonated for 196.10 points**—a new all-time single-week scoring record. Not a narrow escape. Not a lucky Monday-night comeback. An 80.12-point family demolition that turned a rivalry game into a historical document.
Baby Abdo finished with 115.98 points, a total that might have kept him competitive on another Sunday. Against his older brother, it was barely enough to get a seat at the dinner table.

The scene at the Shidid family dinner was reportedly unbearable. Mo climbed onto a chair, lit an enormous celebratory blunt, pointed at his younger brother and delivered the only words anyone would hear for the rest of the night: **“ACKNOWLEDGE ME.”** Abdo, already covered in the metaphorical spaghetti of defeat, could only stare at the scoreboard and wonder how a perfectly ordinary family gathering had become a public execution.

For Mo, this was bigger than finally putting a number in the win column. He came into the season regarded as one of the favorites and spent the first month watching that reputation disintegrate. One record-setting Sunday cannot erase a 1–4 start, but it absolutely changes how opponents will look at his roster. Nobody can dismiss a team capable of dropping nearly 200 points.

For Abdo, the damage goes beyond the standings. He is also 1–4, he just surrendered a league record to his own brother, and his desperate campaign to get Josh Jacobs back has become the family’s second-most-discussed crisis. At this point, the kid may need a trade, a miracle, and a new place to eat Thanksgiving dinner.
stories.headline: The Shidid family massacre! Mo makes history and demands the league acknowledge him

press: ACKNOWLEDGE ME. Four weeks of disrespect, and now everybody knows whose table this is.

For now, the throne belongs to Mo.

body: For four weeks, Sgt. Bob ruled the league like a five-star general who had never heard the word defeat. His troops were organized, his record was spotless, and his undefeated army marched into Week 5 expecting another helpless opponent to surrender.

Unfortunately for Bob, Tyler didn't arrive to negotiate a ceasefire. He arrived with a Manchester City cap, Pep Guardiola on the sideline, and an offense ready to turn a military operation into a demolition site.

Tyler unleashed **163.94 points**, defeating Bob's 121.76 by **42.18 points**. The result delivered Tyler his **third consecutive victory**, pushed his record to 3–2, and handed the previously undefeated general his first loss of the season.

The victory was powered by a three-man offensive air raid. **Bucky Irving erupted for 31.50 points**, **Jared Goff delivered 28.94**, and **George Pickens added 28.00**. Together they scored **88.44 points**—a relentless assault that left Bob's defensive game plan in ruins.

Bob had some soldiers who showed up for duty: **Jaxon Smith-Njigba posted 22.80 points** and **Kyren Williams contributed 19.60**. But the reinforcements never arrived. **Dalton Kincaid scored 3.70**, **Deebo Samuel managed 2.50**, and **Alvin Kamara produced just 2.60**. That trio combined for a miserable **8.80 points** while Tyler's stars were lighting up the scoreboard.

Tyler began the season 0–2 after two agonizing defeats. Three straight wins later, he's 3–2, has just taken down the league's undefeated general, and looks like a contender nobody wants to draw. Bob remains 4–1 and a serious championship threat, but his aura of invincibility is gone. The army can be beaten—and Tyler just published the battle plans.

body: At 1 p.m. Sunday, Zach decided he had already won. The self-proclaimed Trade God looked at an early lead over Hogies and announced, with the confidence of a man who had apparently never watched a full NFL Sunday: **“It feels good to win.”**
The only issue was that an entire afternoon, Sunday night, and Monday night of football remained. Zach had delivered the victory speech before the game had finished its first act.

By the time the dust settled, Hogies had escaped with a **111.64–106.30 win**. The league had witnessed an extraordinary four-stage transformation: smug confidence, nervous laughter, full clown makeup, and finally silence.

Hogies did not need a record-breaking performance. He needed the right players to step up—and, perhaps more importantly, Zach to keep talking. **Kicker Jason Myers erupted for 23.00 points**, a ridiculous total from a position that rarely gets to be the headline. **Trey McBride added 21.60**, while **Christian McCaffrey supplied 17.30**. Those three alone accounted for **61.90 points**, more than half of Hogies’ final total.

Zach had stars of his own. **Joe Burrow led the team with 24.60**, **D’Andre Swift delivered 17.30**, and **Bijan Robinson contributed 15.80**. But the supporting cast turned the Trade God’s celebration into a funeral procession: **David Montgomery scored 1.10, Carnell Tate 1.60, Romeo Doubs 2.60, TreVeyon Henderson 4.80, and the Steelers defense 1.00**. Five lineup spots produced just **11.10 points combined**.

By Sunday night, Hogies had reached **111.64** while Zach was stranded at **98.50**. Monday offered one last chance at salvation. Zach crept to **106.30**, but finished **5.34 points short**. Hogies moved to 4–1; Zach fell to 3–2 with a second straight defeat and the most replayed premature victory speech in league history.

body: Four games into the season, the defending champion looked less like a reigning king and more like a man selling his championship ring on Facebook Marketplace. Shmoody was 0–4, his title defense was collapsing, and the rest of the league was already writing the obituary.
Across the field stood Sean Wavy: inaugural champion, unbeaten at 4–0, and convinced his latest title campaign would be a coronation. Instead, the former king walked into a police sting.

Shmoody finally delivered the performance everyone had been waiting for, hammering Sean **147.78 to 107.32**. A **40.46-point** rout ended Sean’s perfect start and gave the defending champion his first victory. In the Gazette’s official crime-scene reconstruction, Officer Shmoody arrested Sean for fraudulent championship claims and seized the allegedly counterfeit ring as evidence.

The rescue operation had several heroes. **Mike Evans erupted for 26.30 points**, **Jacoby Brissett added 25.28**, **Brock Bowers supplied 23.00**, and **James Cook contributed 22.80**. Those four combined for **97.38 points**, turning a desperate must-win into a public humiliation of the league’s last unbeaten former champion.

Sean did get **27.32 points from Matthew Stafford**, but the supporting cast fell apart. **CeeDee Lamb scored only 2.90**, **Jonathan Taylor managed 11.20**, **Will Shipley posted 8.30**, and the **Cowboys defense finished at minus 2.00**. Kenneth Walker’s bye did not help. When your star receiver barely shows up and your defense actively subtracts points, the undefeated record starts looking very temporary.

The aftermath was every bit as dramatic as the scoreboard. Shmoody reportedly removed his 2025 championship ring from Facebook Marketplace and celebrated by burning a Florian Wirtz jersey. Sean, meanwhile, must explain how a 4–0 juggernaut was dismantled by the one manager everybody had already buried. The defending champion is still only 1–4, but for one glorious week he reminded the league why he wears the crown.

body: They laughed at the draft. They questioned the roster. They said Tyriese had built a fantasy football team that belonged at the bottom of the ocean. Five weeks later, the same manager is standing on the bow of the Going Merry, wearing a straw hat, and shouting to the entire league: **“I’M GONNA BE KING OF THE FANTASY MANAGERS!”**

This was no ordinary win. Tyriese unleashed **180.34 points** against Collin’s 115.20, delivering a **65.14-point beatdown** and moving to 3–2. The preseason punchline has become one of the most explosive teams in the league, and the rest of the managers suddenly have very little to laugh about.
Collin entered the matchup hoping to steady a season that had already been full of frustration. Instead, he ran directly into a pirate ship loaded with touchdowns.

**Puka Nacua led the raid with 37.70 points**, and he had plenty of company. **Davante Adams scored 22.10**, **Derrick Henry supplied 21.00**, **C.J. Stroud delivered 20.94**, and **Sam LaPorta added 19.80**. Even the supporting cast got involved: **Ka’imi Fairbairn kicked in 17.00** and the **Texans defense added 16.00**. It was less a lineup than an entire pirate crew firing cannons at the same target.

Collin had one genuine superstar performance: **Jahmyr Gibbs erupted for 37.70 points**, matching Puka at the top of the individual scoring sheet. **Aaron Rodgers contributed 22.00** and **Braelon Allen delivered 18.60**. But a handful of starters were practically invisible. **Roman Wilson scored 0.00, Tre Harris 3.60, Harold Fannin Jr. 1.40, and T.J. Hockenson 1.70**. Those four combined for just **6.70 points**, wiping out much of Gibbs’s heroic effort.

For Tyriese, this is a second straight win and a full-blown transformation from draft-night joke to championship threat. For Collin, now 2–3, the message is simple: one superstar cannot carry an entire crew when half the ship has fallen overboard.

body: Most people celebrate their wedding weekend with a cake, a first dance, and a few speeches. Tim apparently decided those traditions were not enough. He added a **160.94-point fantasy football explosion** and a win over Marissa, because nothing says newlywed bliss quite like demolishing somebody else’s Sunday.

The Coffey Shop was serving touchdowns all weekend. Tim moved to **3–2** with a **23.60-point victory**, while Marissa dropped to **1–4** despite posting an impressive **137.34**. On most weeks, that is a score worth celebrating. Against the groom, it was just another piece of wedding cake.

The wedding party had plenty of MVPs. **Christian Watson erupted for 32.30 points**, **Parker Washington followed with 30.40**, and kicker **Spencer Shrader supplied a ridiculous 21.00**. Those three alone combined for **83.70 points**. **Trevor Lawrence added 21.74** and **Matthew Golden contributed 20.30**, leaving Marissa chasing a reception hall full of touchdowns.

Marissa did not go quietly. **Drake Maye exploded for 39.46 points**, the biggest individual score in this matchup. **Garrett Wilson added 23.40**, and the **Broncos defense scored 17.00**. **Bhayshul Tuten delivered 11.60** and **Wan’Dale Robinson 11.30**. But **Chris Rodriguez (2.10)**, **Marvin Wilson (7.28)**, and **Mike Gesicki (7.40)** could not keep pace with Tim’s entire wedding party.

Somewhere in South Park, the kids are eating a giant wedding cake marked 160.94 while Cartman screams about a Starbucks burning down. That image pretty much sums up Marissa’s season: enough offense to make things interesting, followed by something catching fire at the worst possible moment.

body: In the Shidid family, Baby Abdo has always sat at the end of the table. Mo is the oldest. Shmoody is the one with the ring, the 2025 champion who beat Tyler 173.30 to 107.30 in the final. Abdo is the one they tell to clear the plates.

That pecking order took a beating last week. Mo dropped a league-record **196.10** on Abdo and spent the night demanding to be acknowledged. Abdo went into Week 6 on a three-game losing streak, last in the league in points scored, with the middle brother next on the schedule.

These two had split their history 1–1. Shmoody took the Week 1 opener in 2025, **160.08 to 130.56**. Abdo answered in Week 12, **129.18 to 102.86**. Then Shmoody went on to win the title while Abdo was knocked out in the quarterfinals. Week 6 was the rubber match, and the whole family was watching.
Little brother won it. Abdo beat Shmoody **118.64 to 113.34**. Oscar picked Shmoody 124–108, and Shmoody closed as an **11.5-point favorite**. Abdo now leads the all-time series **2–1**.

The win came from the players Abdo got from Tyler in their trade last Thursday. **DK Metcalf scored 20.30** and **George Pickens added 13.30**. **Jordan Love scored 20.24**, including a rushing touchdown, and **Dameon Pierce added 15.00** from the flex. Abdo won even with **Darren Waller scoring 0.00** at tight end and **Keenan Allen's 16.20** on his bench.

Shmoody had the bigger names. **James Cook ran for 24.30**, **Bryce Young delivered 19.84** and **Chris Boswell kicked 17.00**. His lineup choices cost him. **Cam Skattebo scored 0.00** in the flex while **Jakobi Meyers put up 13.30** on the bench. That swap alone would have won the game. The **Chiefs D/ST scored 15.00** on the bench while the Panthers D/ST he started managed 6.00. He left **47.60 points** on his bench in a game he lost by 5.30.

It's a painful pattern for the champion. Shmoody has lost to Hogies by **0.38**, to Collin by **5.42** and now to his little brother by **5.30**. He's 1–5, and three of those losses came by less than a touchdown.
Abdo is 2–4 and out of last place. Shmoody is 1–5 and will hear about this at every family meal. One score is still unsettled: Abdo against Mo is the rematch the family really wants.

A week ago Tim got married and dropped **160.94** on Marissa. A week ago the General lost for the first time all season, 163.94 to 121.76 against Tyler. Bob spent the week promising the troops had been retrained and that the honeymoon would end at 1300 hours. It didn't.
Tim won **125.44 to 102.86**, a **22.58-point** ambush as a 9-point underdog. Oscar picked Bob 141–133. The General never got close to either number.

**Christian Watson**, Tim's best man after his 32.30 at the wedding, only managed **9.40**, so the rest of the party picked it up. **Trevor Lawrence threw for 27.34**. **Matthew Golden scored 22.40** and **Emeka Egbuka 17.80**, both from the flex. **Ashton Jeanty added 15.80.** That's back-to-back wins for the Coffey Shop and **four wins in six weeks**.

The slide is real. In his first four weeks, Bob averaged **153.64 points** and went 4–0, including two games over 164. In the last two, he's averaged **112.31** and lost both. He came into the week leading the league in points scored. He now sits fourth.

body: Tyler taught Hogies this game: how to read a waiver wire, how to work a trade, how to sleep through a 1 p.m. kickoff without checking his phone. On Sunday, the student handed the teacher his worst score of the season.

The gap between them used to be enormous. In 2025 Tyler went **10–4**, scored **1,914.82 points** and reached the championship game before Shmoody beat him 173.30 to 107.30. Hogies went **6–8** and spent December in the toilet bowl, where he at least won the final and handed the trophy to Ryan. When they met in Week 11, the master won **144.80 to 94.02**.

That was last year. Hogies has started 2026 at **5–1**, and his only loss was a 162.88 to 156.30 shootout with Tyriese. Tyler came into Sunday on a three-game winning streak, fresh off ending Bob's perfect season and declaring a national holiday.

The holiday is over. Hogies won **134.32 to 88.52**, a **45.80-point** beating, and their all-time series is now **1–1**. Oscar picked Hogies 139–117. The line moved from Hogies −24.5 at the open to **−56** at kickoff, so the teacher technically covered. That is the only good news in this story.

Tyler's lineup was gutted before the game. **Six of his eight bench players were on bye**: Jared Goff and Amon-Ra St. Brown with Detroit, Aaron Jones, Jordan Mason and the Vikings D/ST with Minnesota, and Tee Higgins with Cincinnati. His whole bench scored **0.00**. He did remember his first lesson and traded for **Aaron Rodgers**, who covered Goff's bye with **16.02**. **Luther Burden led the team with 17.50** and **Jalen Coker added 15.70**, but **Juwan Johnson scored 0.00** at tight end and **Tyjae Spears managed 1.80** before Tyler cut him. **Bucky Irving**, Oscar's TD pick for Tyler, had already been traded to Abdo.

The student didn't need to do much. **Christian McCaffrey scored 30.70** with two touchdowns, **Chuba Hubbard added 19.10** and **Carnell Tate caught 19.00**. Hogies won by 45 with **Tyler Shough's 26.96 sitting on his bench** behind Dak Prescott's 11.02.

Hogies is tied with Sean for the league lead. Tyler is 3–3, still seventh, and holds the last playoff spot. Last December, Tyler played for a title while Hogies played for pride. This year, the student is at the front of the class.

body: One year ago this week, Tyriese beat Sean **104.64 to 100.66**. On Sunday, in Week 6 again, Sean got his revenge, and he did it with the highest score in the league.

These two have traded places in a hurry. Sean won the league's first championship in 2024, then crashed to **2–12** in 2025. That same year, Tyriese went **9–5** and reached the playoffs before Shmoody knocked him out. This preseason, everyone laughed at Tyriese's draft. Five weeks later, he was standing on the bow of the Going Merry in a straw hat, calling himself the king of the fantasy managers.

Sean had his own drama. Last week he filed a missing person report for Kenneth Walker, who was simply on bye, and lost his perfect season to Shmoody. This week the case was solved. **Walker scored 27.90 with two touchdowns** and led Sean's team.

Sean won **145.28 to 113.78**, a **31.50-point** win that more than doubled the 15.5-point spread. Oscar picked Sean 146–133 and almost nailed his number. **Jonathan Taylor added 21.10**, **Tyler Bass kicked 17.00**, **Matthew Stafford threw for 16.88** and **CeeDee Lamb caught 16.00**. Even the **Jaguars D/ST's −2.00** couldn't slow him down.

The King's crew let him down. **C.J. Stroud scored 22.98** and **Colston Loveland 18.50**, but **Puka Nacua**, Oscar's TD pick with the highest projection in the game, managed **14.00** and no touchdown. **Derrick Henry scored 5.00** and **Davante Adams 6.90**. **Stefon Diggs scored 16.40** on the bench, and **75.72 points** sat there in total.

Their series is now **1–1**. Sean is 5–1, tied with Hogies for the league lead, and his **870.68 points** are the most in the league. Tyriese is 3–3 and still holds the sixth playoff spot. The King is still at sea. He just learned that the former champion isn't finished.

body: A year ago these two were living in different worlds. Marissa went **10–4** in 2025, scored **1,885.46 points** and made the playoffs. Mo went **4–10**. When they met in Week 5, Marissa won **161.62 to 112.54**.

This year the roles have flipped. Before kickoff, Marissa looked at Mo's league-record 196.10 and said she'd rather talk about getting to 2–4. She was right that somebody was getting to 2–4. It just wasn't her.

Mo won **139.50 to 119.60** with **Ja'Marr Chase and Justin Jefferson both on bye**. That's two straight wins after an 0–4 start, and he covered the 7.5-point spread. Oscar picked Mo 129–124. The series is now **1–1**.

Mo's backups stepped up. **Malik Nabers caught 28.50**, **Tre Tucker added 26.70** and **Isaiah Likely posted 23.90** at tight end. **Josh Allen threw for 18.30** but didn't run one in, so Oscar's TD pick missed. Mo's **843.76 points** are the third most in the league, which makes his 2–4 record look like a misprint. Three of his four losses came against teams that are now 4–2 or 5–1.

Marissa did her part at quarterback. She picked **Drake Maye** over **Patrick Mahomes**, and Maye scored **23.80** with a rushing touchdown, one of Oscar's four TD hits. Mahomes scored 10.48 on the bench. **Bhayshul Tuten added 24.70** and the **Broncos D/ST 13.00**. But **Kenny Gainwell**, bought from Zach for $20 one minute before Sunday's kickoff, scored **3.40** in his first start, and **Garrett Wilson managed 8.40**.

It's been that kind of season for Marissa. She has had **862.12 points scored against her**, the most in the league. She lost last week with 137.34. She is 1–5 and has lost two straight, and the spa she opened for her injured players is still fully booked.
Mo is 2–4, eighth in the standings and rolling. Chase and Jefferson come back from vacation this week. Last year's 10–4 team is now chasing last year's 4–10 team, and the gap is growing.

body: Collin and Zach list each other as rivals. Until Sunday they had never played. Collin has made seven trades this season, more than anyone except Tyler. Zach calls himself the Trade God. Their first meeting came down to whose deals paid off.

Zach came in on a two-game losing streak, still wearing the clown makeup from Week 5, when he told the league "it feels good to win" at 1 p.m. and lost to Hogies by midnight. This time he promised to keep quiet until Monday. Mostly, he did.
Zach won **128.80 to 104.98**, a **23.82-point** win. The line opened at **Zach −41** and closed at −27.5, so Collin covered. Oscar picked Zach 143–108.

The Trade God's deals did the work. **George Kittle**, pried away from Shmoody for Devaughn Vele in Week 2, caught **17.90**. **Jayden Daniels**, acquired from Tyler before the season, threw for **21.00**. **D'Andre Swift ran for 23.00**, **Keon Coleman added 15.90** and the **Steelers D/ST scored 12.00**. Zach won comfortably even though **Bijan Robinson**, Oscar's TD pick and the best running back projection of the week, managed **7.30** and no touchdown, and **Brandon Aubrey kicked 1.00**.

Collin's trades went the other way. He was without **Jahmyr Gibbs**, on bye with Detroit, and **Breece Hall**, back on his roster after a round trip through Tyler's, didn't play. At quarterback he started **Jameis Winston**, who scored **6.48**. During Sunday night's game he traded Stefon Diggs to Tyriese for **Kirk Cousins**, who scored **18.52 on Tyriese's bench**. Earlier in the season he sent **Jakobi Meyers** to Shmoody for Justin Herbert, and Meyers is now lighting up the champion's bench.

Collin still had bright spots. **Germie Bernard scored 25.70** and **DeVonta Smith 20.50**. But **A.J. Brown managed 5.70** and **Harold Fannin 1.90**, and the waiver wire he sued last week has still not settled out of court.

Zach is 4–2, fifth in the standings, and leads the head-to-head **1–0**. Collin is 2–4 and has lost two straight. One of them has turned trading into a religion. The other is still waiting for a trade to pay off.

trades.method: Grades compare the combined trade value (FantasyCalc market, Sleeper projections and 2026 production) each side received, on the day Oscar graded it. Quarterbacks count at 40% of their value, since starters are easy to find in this league — except Josh Allen, Joe Burrow and Lamar Jackson, who keep full value. FAAB counts at 0.04 value points per dollar. Trades made before the site launched were graded on Oct 14 with hindsight.

trades.headline: Tyler turns Amon-Ra into three starters

sides.note: Tyler parted with Amon-Ra St. Brown, the WR4, and came home with Zay Flowers (WR9), Nico Collins (WR12) and D'Andre Swift (RB12, 103.8 points), with Kyle Monangai for luggage. One diamond is a lovely thing to own; three good starters are a lovely thing to play, and Tyler has chosen the lineup over the jewellery box.

Zach kept Zay Flowers for barely twelve hours before cashing him, Nico Collins and D'Andre Swift in for Amon-Ra St. Brown, the WR4 and the finest player in the deal. Depth is a comfort, but stars win championships, and Zach has decided he would rather be brilliant than comfortable.

trades.headline: Zach flips Burrow for Zay Flowers

sides.note: seanwavy acquired Joe Burrow, one of only three quarterbacks this league deigns to value, but paid with Zay Flowers, the WR9 with 94.5 points to his name. DJ Moore has managed 36.3 points and Zach Charbonnet none at all; one should never exchange a reliable present for a merely interesting future.

Zach surrendered a premium quarterback and two hopes for Zay Flowers, the WR9, and Matthew Stafford, whose 111.86 points rather outshine Burrow's 104.24. To lose Joe Burrow looks like carelessness; to replace him with a cheaper man who has scored more looks suspiciously like wisdom.

trades.headline: Collin swaps Diggs for Kirk Cousins

sides.note: Collin gave up Stefon Diggs for Kirk Cousins, a quarterback in a league where quarterbacks are as plentiful as excuses. Cousins did score 18.52 on Sunday while Jameis Winston managed 6.48 for Collin, but one good afternoon on another man's bench is a flirtation, not a marriage.

Tyriese turned a bench quarterback into Stefon Diggs, a receiver with 53 points this season and two 15-plus weeks to his name. To lose a backup quarterback is a misfortune in most leagues; in this one it is merely housekeeping.

Zach let Kenny Gainwell go for $20 of waiver money, and money, however charming, has never scored a point on a Sunday. Still, Gainwell had spent three weeks on Zach's bench, so this was less a loss than a tidying of the wardrobe.

Marissa paid $20 for Kenny Gainwell, a modest back with 30.2 points this season and a projection of about nine a week. He went straight into her lineup and produced 3.4 — but one should never judge a purchase by its first outing, only by its price, and the price was low.

trades.headline: Tyler cashes in four for Amon-Ra

sides.note: Tyler sent four players out the door and came home with Amon-Ra St. Brown, the WR5 on the trade market with 104.2 points already, plus Jeremiyah Love and $10. One star is worth a crowd only if the crowd was mediocre; this crowd was a shade better, so the grade falls just short of the glamour.

Abdo gave up the brightest receiver in the deal for Bucky Irving (RB16), George Pickens (WR17), Jameson Williams and DK Metcalf. Quantity is the refuge of those who cannot afford quality, but with two flex spots to fill, Abdo can at least afford a full lineup.

trades.headline: Rodgers rides in for Goff’s bye

sides.note: Tyler, with Jared Goff on bye, bought Aaron Rodgers and was paid $18 to take him — a quarterback projected for 15.9 this week is a fine thing to borrow. But Brian Robinson was worth a shade more, and in this league a spare quarterback is the one luxury everyone already owns.

Collin parted with a quarterback and $18 for Brian Robinson, a running back with 50.1 points to his name. To give away what is easily replaced and receive what is not is the whole art of commerce, even when the receipt is modest.
Tyler sold Kaelon Black for $20 of FAAB. Small stakes, small grade.
Hogies spent $20 on a handcuff for Christian McCaffrey. Insurance is boring until the house burns down.
Tyler sent Breece Hall back where he came from and came away with three contributors. Aaron Jones put up 18.7 in the Week 5 win over Bob.
Collin got Breece Hall back, which is either a correction or an admission. Braelon Allen gave him 18.6 in Week 5.
Marissa paid $100 of FAAB and a starting quarterback to get a different starting quarterback. In this league that is like buying sand at the beach.
In a one-quarterback league, quarterbacks are cheap, and Tim knew it. He moved Mahomes, kept a starter in Bo Nix and pocketed $100 of FAAB for the trouble.
Tyler reacquired Marvin Harrison, who has since been traded to Houston, and added Braelon Allen for RJ Harvey. Two for one is a decent afternoon.
Baby Abdo consolidated two pieces into RJ Harvey, a reasonable flex play. The value went slightly the other way.
Collin gave up a receiver for a quarterback in a league where quarterbacks grow on trees. Herbert has since left his roster, which rather proves the point.
Jakobi Meyers is only a bench piece, but Shmoody turned a replaceable quarterback into a receiver who can fill a flex spot. A quiet win.
Two starters for Alvin Kamara. Collin finally won a trade, and he won it cleanly.
Bob traded two players for Alvin Kamara, who produced 2.6 points in Week 5. The General’s intelligence services have failed him.

trades.headline: Jefferson and Warren for Bucky and Pickens

sides.note: On paper Mo got the bigger names. On the field, Bucky Irving and George Pickens combined for 59.5 points in Week 5 and powered the win over Bob. The grade says C; the scoreboard disagrees.
Mo collected Justin Jefferson and Jaylen Warren, and Warren’s 36.8 helped set the league record. Jefferson’s bye this week is the only blemish.
Tee Higgins and Jalen Coker are fine receivers. Zay Flowers is a better one, and Tyler gave him up along with a running back.
Zay Flowers has become a top-ten receiver on the market. Sean keeps beating Tyler in trades; perhaps he should start charging admission.

Collin sent away Lamar Jackson, one of the three quarterbacks in this league actually worth paying for, but came back with three useful bodies in Hurts, Diggs and Bateman. Depth is a consolation prize, though not a worthless one.
Baby Abdo landed Lamar Jackson, one of the league's rare quarterbacks who changes a week on his own, plus Marvin Harrison before his move to Houston. Lamar carries this grade by himself.
George Kittle for Devaughn Vele is the kind of trade that earns a man the name Trade God. Kittle is a top-three tight end by market value.
The defending champion swapped an elite tight end for a backup receiver. Some champions defend their crown; Shmoody appears to have pawned it.
Breece Hall was the prize, and Tyler turned three pieces into a starting running back and a receiver. Quality over quantity, for once.
Collin took the volume, but Harrison and Kamara were both traded on within a week. DeVonta Smith is the only piece still standing.
Days after acquiring Kenneth Walker, Tyler sent him back to Sean for three depth pieces. Walker has since become one of the most valuable players in the league. Oscar has no further questions.
Sean lost Walker, then got him back with Kyler Murray attached. The rare trade where the victim of the first robbery writes the sequel.
Tyler swapped one ordinary quarterback for another and collected $30 of FAAB for his trouble. In this league that's a fair deal.
Zach paid $30 to swap Kyler Murray for Jayden Daniels, two quarterbacks this league treats as interchangeable. No harm done, and little gained.
Tyler surrendered Josh Allen, now the top quarterback in fantasy, for Jayden Daniels and Marvin Harrison, who has since been traded to Houston. Ten FAAB dollars do not buy forgiveness.
Mo walked away with Josh Allen, who threw for 30.5 points in the record-breaking 196-point week. Jonathon Brooks was a lottery ticket; Allen was the jackpot.
Two useful receivers out the door for a rookie running back who gave the Trade God 4.8 points in Week 5. Even gods have off days.
Denzel Boston has turned into a weekly starter and Deebo Samuel adds depth. The General recruited two soldiers for the price of one.

trades.headline: Walker for Lamb, and Tyler wins the swap

sides.note: Kenneth Walker is now the fourth-most valuable player in fantasy, and Tyler got Jameson Williams thrown in. A splendid piece of business, undone only by what Tyler did next.
CeeDee Lamb is a fine receiver, but giving up a top-five running back for him looks worse every week. Tyjae Spears does not change the arithmetic.
